meta.mutcd_note: Codes are MUTCD sign designations (R/W/S/M/I/D series) or MUTCD section references for signals and pavement markings.

regulatory_signs.name: Stop
regulatory_signs.meaning: Come to a complete stop before the stop line or crosswalk. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Slowing without a full stop is illegal.

regulatory_signs.name: Stop — Except Right Turn
regulatory_signs.meaning: Used in conjunction with a stop sign. Motorists may make a right turn without stopping.

regulatory_signs.name: Stop — 4-Way
regulatory_signs.meaning: All four approaches have stop signs. First vehicle to arrive goes first. Simultaneous arrival: yield to vehicle on the right.

regulatory_signs.name: Yield
regulatory_signs.meaning: Slow down and give right-of-way to pedestrians and approaching traffic. Stop only if necessary. You must have a sufficient gap before proceeding.

regulatory_signs.name: Yield to Oncoming Traffic
regulatory_signs.meaning: Used with yield signs at one-lane bridges or underpasses. You must yield right-of-way to opposing traffic.

regulatory_signs.name: Railroad Crossbuck
regulatory_signs.meaning: Treat as a Yield sign. Slow down and prepare to stop if you see or hear a train approaching.

regulatory_signs.name: Do Not Enter
regulatory_signs.meaning: Do not drive onto this street or ramp from your direction. Often posted at the beginning of one-way streets and highway ramps.

regulatory_signs.name: Wrong Way
regulatory_signs.meaning: You are traveling in the wrong direction. Posted farther down the wrong-way street to catch drivers who missed the Do Not Enter sign. Turn around safely.

regulatory_signs.name: One Way
regulatory_signs.meaning: Traffic flows in one direction only — the direction the arrow points. Turning onto a one-way street in the wrong direction could cause a head-on collision.

regulatory_signs.name: Divided Highway
regulatory_signs.meaning: The road you are on intersects a divided highway — two one-way roadways separated by a median. At the first roadway, turn right only; at the second, turn left only.

regulatory_signs.name: No Trucks
regulatory_signs.meaning: Trucks may not use this roadway.

regulatory_signs.name: No Bicycles
regulatory_signs.meaning: Bicycles may not use this roadway.

regulatory_signs.name: No Pedestrian Crossing
regulatory_signs.meaning: Pedestrians may not cross at this location.

regulatory_signs.name: No U-Turn
regulatory_signs.meaning: U-turns are prohibited at this location. Do not make a complete turn to go in the opposite direction.

regulatory_signs.name: No Right Turn
regulatory_signs.meaning: Right turns are prohibited at this intersection.

regulatory_signs.name: No Left Turn
regulatory_signs.meaning: Left turns are prohibited at this intersection.

regulatory_signs.name: No Parking
regulatory_signs.meaning: You may not park a vehicle at this location. Stopping briefly to pick up or drop off a passenger may be permitted.

regulatory_signs.name: Do Not Pass
regulatory_signs.meaning: Passing vehicles ahead is not permitted in this area. Often accompanied by the yellow No Passing Zone pennant sign.

regulatory_signs.name: No Turn on Red
regulatory_signs.meaning: You may not turn in the indicated direction during a red light cycle at this intersection. You must wait for a green signal.

regulatory_signs.name: Keep Right
regulatory_signs.meaning: Drivers must stay to the right of a traffic island, divider, or obstruction.

regulatory_signs.name: Speed Limit 65
regulatory_signs.meaning: Maximum legal speed is 65 mph under ideal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions require it.

regulatory_signs.name: Reserved Parking (Disabled)
regulatory_signs.meaning: Parking reserved for vehicles displaying valid disabled person placards or registration plates. Unauthorized parking results in fines and towing.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Left Turn or Straight
regulatory_signs.meaning: If you are in this lane, you may turn left or continue straight through the intersection.

regulatory_signs.name: Center Lane — Left Turn Only
regulatory_signs.meaning: This lane is reserved exclusively for left-turning vehicles traveling in either direction. Do not use for through traffic or passing.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Turn Left or Right
regulatory_signs.meaning: You may turn in either direction the arrows point from this lane.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Straight or Right Turn
regulatory_signs.meaning: You may go straight or turn right from this lane.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Turn Right Only
regulatory_signs.meaning: You must turn right at the intersection. You may not continue straight even if you are in this lane by mistake.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Turn Left Only
regulatory_signs.meaning: You must turn left at the intersection. You may not continue straight even if you are in this lane by mistake.

regulatory_signs.name: Left Turn Yield on Flashing Yellow Arrow
regulatory_signs.meaning: A left turn is permitted when the flashing yellow arrow is displayed, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Your turn is NOT protected.

regulatory_signs.name: Left Turn Yield on Green
regulatory_signs.meaning: Left turns are permitted on green but you must yield to oncoming traffic. Your turn is not protected by a dedicated arrow.

regulatory_signs.name: Opposing Traffic Has Extended Green
regulatory_signs.meaning: After your signal turns red, opposing traffic may continue moving for a brief period. Do not proceed until it is safe.

regulatory_signs.name: Lane Use — Right Turn Signal
regulatory_signs.meaning: This lane is designated for right-turning vehicles only. If you are in this lane, you must turn right at the upcoming intersection.

warning_signs.name: No Passing Zone
warning_signs.meaning: The only pennant-shaped warning sign. Marks the beginning of a no-passing zone. Posted on the left side of the road facing the driver.

warning_signs.name: Chevron — Left
warning_signs.meaning: Sharp change in road direction to the left. Road bends the direction the chevron points. Often placed throughout curves for additional guidance.

warning_signs.name: Chevron — Right
warning_signs.meaning: Sharp change in road direction to the right. Road bends the direction the chevron points.

warning_signs.name: Left Curve Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: The road curves to the left. Slow down, stay in the center of your lane, and prepare to navigate the left-bending curve.

warning_signs.name: Right Curve Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: The road curves to the right. Slow down and position your vehicle slightly right of center as you drive through.

warning_signs.name: Sharp Left Turn
warning_signs.meaning: The road turns sharply to the left. Slow down substantially. May have an advisory speed on the sign or posted below it.

warning_signs.name: Sharp Right Turn
warning_signs.meaning: The road turns sharply to the right. Slow down substantially. Position slightly right of center.

warning_signs.name: Set of Curves — First Left
warning_signs.meaning: A set of two curves — the first bending left, the second bending right. Slow down and prepare to navigate both.

warning_signs.name: Set of Curves — First Right
warning_signs.meaning: A set of two curves — the first bending right, the second bending left.

warning_signs.name: Winding Road
warning_signs.meaning: Three or more curves in a row on the road ahead. Drive carefully and at a reduced speed through the entire section.

warning_signs.name: One Direction Large Arrow
warning_signs.meaning: The road changes direction at an extreme angle. Slow down as much as you would for a turn at an intersection.

warning_signs.name: Road Entering Curve
warning_signs.meaning: The main road curves with a side road entering from the right. A driver preparing to enter may not see you. Approach with extra caution.

warning_signs.name: Truck Rollover
warning_signs.meaning: This curve has a high risk of truck rollover when traveled at excessive speeds. Truck drivers should reduce speed significantly.

warning_signs.name: Advisory Speed Sign
warning_signs.meaning: Used with any diamond-shaped warning sign. Indicates the highest safe speed (in this example, 25 mph) to travel through the upcoming hazard.

warning_signs.name: Merging Traffic
warning_signs.meaning: Traffic from another roadway or ramp is merging into your lane. Entering traffic must yield to traffic already on the major roadway.

warning_signs.name: Added Lane
warning_signs.meaning: Two roadways are meeting, but merging is not required because a new lane has been added. Entering traffic uses the new lane.

warning_signs.name: Weave Area
warning_signs.meaning: You will be merging with another roadway while some traffic is exiting and crossing your path. Use caution.

warning_signs.name: Divided Highway Begins
warning_signs.meaning: The highway ahead becomes divided with a median separating traffic. Keep to the right of the divider.

warning_signs.name: Divided Highway Ends
warning_signs.meaning: The divided highway ends ahead. You will be on a two-way road. Keep right and watch for oncoming traffic.

warning_signs.name: Two-Way Traffic Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: The one-way road or street ends and you will be on a two-lane road with traffic moving in both directions. Stay in your lane and keep right of center.

warning_signs.name: Lane Ends
warning_signs.meaning: One lane on a multi-lane road ends ahead. Traffic in the ending lane must merge safely into the continuing lane.

warning_signs.name: Right Lane Ends
warning_signs.meaning: The right lane ends ahead. Drivers in the right lane must merge left. Signal and find a safe gap.

warning_signs.name: Lane Ends — Merge Left
warning_signs.meaning: Your lane ends ahead and you must merge into the lane to the left.

warning_signs.name: Cross Road Intersection
warning_signs.meaning: A cross road intersection is ahead. Approach with caution — traffic may enter from all four directions.

warning_signs.name: Side Road Intersection
warning_signs.meaning: A side road enters from the right ahead. A driver entering from the side road may pull out in front of you.

warning_signs.name: T-Intersection
warning_signs.meaning: The road you are on ends at a T-intersection. You must turn left or right — the road does not continue straight.

warning_signs.name: Y-Intersection
warning_signs.meaning: A Y-shaped intersection ahead. The road splits into two branches.

warning_signs.name: Circular Intersection (Roundabout)
warning_signs.meaning: A roundabout or traffic circle is ahead. Yield to traffic already in the circle. Travel counterclockwise.

warning_signs.name: Two-Direction Large Arrow
warning_signs.meaning: Posted at the far side of a T-intersection. You can only go left or right — the road does not continue straight through.

warning_signs.name: Narrow Bridge or Underpass Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: The bridge or underpass ahead is narrower than the road. Lanes become narrower and there is generally no shoulder. Stay in your lane.

warning_signs.name: Slippery When Wet
warning_signs.meaning: Road surface is especially slippery in wet weather. Reduce speed, increase following distance, and avoid quick acceleration or braking.

warning_signs.name: Deer Crossing
warning_signs.meaning: Deer frequently cross in this area and crashes with deer have occurred. Be alert especially at dawn and dusk.

warning_signs.name: Low Clearance
warning_signs.meaning: An underpass, tunnel, or parking garage has limited height. If your vehicle is taller than the posted clearance, do not enter.

warning_signs.name: Low Shoulder
warning_signs.meaning: The shoulder is lower than the road surface by up to 3 inches. If you drift onto the shoulder, do not brake or steer sharply — ease back gently.

warning_signs.name: Shoulder Drop-Off
warning_signs.meaning: Severe drop-off where the shoulder meets the road edge. Drifting off the pavement could cause loss of vehicle control.

warning_signs.name: Soft Shoulder
warning_signs.meaning: The shoulder is unpaved and soft. If you drive on it, your vehicle may sink in. Do not use the soft shoulder as a travel lane.

warning_signs.name: Hill / Downgrade
warning_signs.meaning: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and reduce brake wear.

warning_signs.name: Traffic Signal Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: A traffic signal is at the intersection ahead that you may not be able to see due to a curve, hill, or obstruction. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

warning_signs.name: Stop Sign Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: A stop sign at the intersection ahead may not be visible due to a curve or hill. Slow down and prepare to stop completely.

warning_signs.name: Bicycle Crossing Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: Bicyclists may be crossing your path ahead. Be prepared to slow down if necessary and give cyclists at least 4 feet of clearance.

warning_signs.name: Railroad Crossing Ahead
warning_signs.meaning: A railroad crossing is ahead — the only circular warning sign. Begin looking and listening for a train. Be prepared to stop.

warning_signs.name: Advanced Intersection / Railroad Crossing
warning_signs.meaning: The intersecting road has a railroad crossing very close to this intersection. If planning to turn and a train is approaching, be prepared to stop.

warning_signs.name: Share the Road — Bicycle/Motor Vehicle
warning_signs.meaning: Used at roadway pinch points (no shoulder, narrow lanes) to warn motorists to provide adequate space for bicyclists sharing the road.

warning_signs.name: Pedestrian Crossing
warning_signs.meaning: Used at or before locations where pedestrians may cross. Be prepared to slow down or stop. Yield to all pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk.

warning_signs.name: School Zone / School Crossing
warning_signs.meaning: The only pentagon-shaped sign on roadways. Approaching a school zone. Slow to 15 mph when children are present or when flashing lights are active.

warning_signs.name: Horse-Drawn Vehicle
warning_signs.meaning: Slow-moving horse-drawn vehicles (such as Amish buggies) cross or share the roadway in this area. Slow down and give them plenty of space.

warning_signs.name: Set of Sharp Turns — First Right
warning_signs.meaning: A set of two sharp turns is ahead, the first bending sharply to the right and the second to the left. Slow down substantially before reaching the first turn.

warning_signs.name: Set of Sharp Turns — First Left
warning_signs.meaning: A set of two sharp turns is ahead, the first bending sharply to the left and the second to the right. Slow down substantially before reaching the first turn.

work_zone_signs.name: Work Zone — Turn On Headlights
work_zone_signs.meaning: PA state law requires headlights on at all times in posted work zones. Failure to comply results in an additional $25 fine.

work_zone_signs.name: Active Work Zone — When Flashing
work_zone_signs.meaning: An active work zone where construction, maintenance, or utility workers are on or near the roadway. Increased fines apply.

work_zone_signs.name: End Active Work Zone
work_zone_signs.meaning: The active work zone has ended. Normal speed limits and fines resume beyond this sign.

work_zone_signs.name: Road Work Ahead
work_zone_signs.meaning: Road work is ahead. Slow down, be alert, and be prepared for changing traffic patterns, narrow lanes, and workers near the road.

work_zone_signs.name: Road Closed — Flooding
work_zone_signs.meaning: The road is closed due to flooding. Use an alternate route. Never attempt to drive through flooded roads — Turn Around Don't Drown.

work_zone_signs.name: Right Lane Closed Ahead
work_zone_signs.meaning: The right lane will be closed at a specified distance ahead. Merge into the open lane as soon as it is safe to do so.

work_zone_signs.name: Workers Ahead
work_zone_signs.meaning: Workers are on or very close to the roadway. Slow down and take special care. Highway workers can report unsafe drivers to police.

work_zone_signs.name: Flagger Ahead
work_zone_signs.meaning: A flagger (flag person) is controlling traffic ahead. Follow flagger instructions — their authority overrides conventional traffic control devices.

work_zone_signs.name: Flagger — Stop Paddle
work_zone_signs.meaning: When a flagger displays the STOP paddle (or red flag), all traffic must stop and wait.

work_zone_signs.name: Flagger — Slow Paddle
work_zone_signs.meaning: When a flagger displays the SLOW paddle, reduce speed and proceed carefully through the work zone.

work_zone_signs.name: Electronic Arrow Panel — Move/Merge Right
work_zone_signs.meaning: Large electronic flashing arrow panel indicating drivers should move or merge to the right. Begin merge well in advance.

work_zone_signs.name: Electronic Arrow Panel — Move/Merge Left
work_zone_signs.meaning: Electronic flashing arrow panel indicating drivers should move or merge to the left.

work_zone_signs.name: Electronic Arrow Panel — Caution
work_zone_signs.meaning: A caution pattern on the arrow panel indicates a work area is adjacent to the travel lane. Drive with extra caution.

work_zone_signs.name: Channeling Devices
work_zone_signs.meaning: Barrels, tubes, cones, and vertical panels guide drivers through changing traffic patterns in work zones. Keep away from hazards and stay within the channeled lane.

guide_signs.name: Highway Exit Sign — 2 Miles
guide_signs.meaning: Highway/expressway guide sign indicating an exit is 2 miles ahead. The first of three advance signs posted on highways.

guide_signs.name: Highway Exit Sign — 1 Mile
guide_signs.meaning: Second advance highway exit sign — exit is 1 mile ahead. Begin moving toward the correct lane.

guide_signs.name: Highway Exit Sign — At Exit
guide_signs.meaning: The exit ramp is here. Move to the exit lane. Do not cross solid white lines to reach the exit.

guide_signs.name: Exit Only (Left side)
guide_signs.meaning: Your lane exits the highway. You must exit if you stay in this lane. Change lanes now if you want to continue on the highway.

guide_signs.name: Exit Only (Right side)
guide_signs.meaning: This lane exits the highway on the right side. Must exit if staying in lane.

guide_signs.name: Interstate Shield
guide_signs.meaning: Indicates the highway is an interstate. Even-numbered interstates run east-west; odd-numbered run north-south. Three-digit interstates are connectors.

guide_signs.name: U.S. Route Marker
guide_signs.meaning: Indicates you are traveling on a U.S. Traffic Route. The number identifies the specific route.

guide_signs.name: Pennsylvania Keystone Route Marker
guide_signs.meaning: Pennsylvania's unique keystone-shaped marker indicating a Pennsylvania State Traffic Route.

guide_signs.name: Route Junction Plate
guide_signs.meaning: Junction plate on a route marker showing you are approaching the intersection with the indicated route.

guide_signs.name: Route Direction Plate
guide_signs.meaning: Direction plate on a route marker showing the cardinal direction (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH) you are traveling on the route.

guide_signs.name: Mile Markers
guide_signs.meaning: Indicate the number of miles from the point where the traffic route entered the state or its beginning. Numbers increase east or north. Help pinpoint location for roadside assistance.

guide_signs.name: Route Supplemental Arrow
guide_signs.meaning: A supplemental arrow below a route marker assembly shows which direction to turn to continue on the indicated route. Here it means a turn is required to remain on the route.

guide_signs.name: Route Supplemental Arrow — TO
guide_signs.meaning: A TO plate combined with a route marker and supplemental arrow means the indicated route is accessible by continuing ahead — you do not need to turn. The TO plate distinguishes access from continuation.

service_signs.name: Hospital
service_signs.meaning: A hospital is located at the next exit or nearby. Follow H signs to reach emergency medical services.

service_signs.name: Telephone
service_signs.meaning: A public telephone is available at the next exit or nearby location.

service_signs.name: Food
service_signs.meaning: Food service (restaurant, fast food) is available at the next exit.

service_signs.name: Gas
service_signs.meaning: A gasoline service station is available at the next exit.

service_signs.name: Diesel
service_signs.meaning: Diesel fuel is available at the next exit. Important for truck drivers and diesel vehicle operators.

service_signs.name: Lodging
service_signs.meaning: Hotel, motel, or other overnight lodging is available at the next exit.

service_signs.name: Tourist-Oriented Directional Sign (Blue)
service_signs.meaning: Directs motorists to tourist attractions such as museums, historical landmarks, or cultural sites. Blue indicates general tourist services.

service_signs.name: Tourist-Oriented Directional Sign (Brown)
service_signs.meaning: Directs motorists to recreational areas, state or national parks, and historical landmarks. Brown indicates public recreation and cultural interest sites.

traffic_signals.name: Traffic Light — Vertical and Horizontal Layout
traffic_signals.meaning: Traffic signals are arranged vertically (red on top, green on bottom) or horizontally (red on left, green on right).

traffic_signals.name: Steady Red Light
traffic_signals.meaning: Stop completely before the stop line or crosswalk. Wait for a green light. Right turn on red is allowed after a full stop (unless prohibited). Left turn on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

traffic_signals.name: Steady Yellow Light
traffic_signals.meaning: A red light is about to appear. Slow down and prepare to stop. If within the intersection or unable to stop safely, continue through carefully.

traffic_signals.name: Steady Green Light
traffic_signals.meaning: You may proceed through the intersection if the road is clear. You may turn right or left unless a sign prohibits it — yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic when turning.

traffic_signals.name: Steady Red Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: Stop. You may not turn in the direction the arrow points. Wait for a green arrow or flashing yellow arrow before proceeding.

traffic_signals.name: Steady Yellow Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: The green or flashing yellow arrow phase is ending and will turn red. Slow down and prepare to stop completely.

traffic_signals.name: Steady Green Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: You may turn in the direction the arrow points. Your turn is protected — oncoming traffic is stopped by a red light. If the arrow turns to a green light, you may still turn but must yield.

traffic_signals.name: Flashing Red Light
traffic_signals.meaning: Treat as a STOP sign. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

traffic_signals.name: Flashing Yellow Light
traffic_signals.meaning: Caution. Slow down, look, and proceed carefully. You do not need to stop.

traffic_signals.name: Flashing Yellow Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: You may turn in the direction of the arrow but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Your turn is NOT protected — oncoming traffic has a green light.

traffic_signals.name: Lane Use Signal — Green Arrow Down
traffic_signals.meaning: A steady downward green arrow over a traffic lane means you may use that lane.

traffic_signals.name: Lane Use Signal — Yellow X
traffic_signals.meaning: A steady yellow X means the direction of travel in this lane is about to reverse. Change lanes safely and immediately.

traffic_signals.name: Lane Use Signal — Red X
traffic_signals.meaning: A steady red X means you are not allowed to use this traffic lane.

traffic_signals.name: Lane Use Signal — One-Way Left Turn Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: A white one-way left-turn arrow over a lane means you may only turn left from that lane.
traffic_signals.mutcd_code: MUTCD 4L.01 — Lane Control One-Way Left Arrow

traffic_signals.name: Lane Use Signal — Two-Way Left Turn Arrow
traffic_signals.meaning: A white two-way left-turn arrow means you may only turn left, but the lane is shared with left-turning drivers from the opposite direction.
traffic_signals.mutcd_code: MUTCD 4L.01 — Lane Control Two-Way Left Arrow

traffic_signals.name: Pedestrian Signal — WALK
traffic_signals.meaning: When the WALK signal or walking person symbol appears, pedestrians may start crossing. Remain alert for turning vehicles.

traffic_signals.name: Pedestrian Signal — Walking Person
traffic_signals.meaning: The illuminated walking person symbol indicates pedestrians may cross. Same meaning as WALK.

traffic_signals.name: Pedestrian Signal — Flashing DON'T WALK
traffic_signals.meaning: If you have started crossing, finish crossing. If you have not left the curb, do not start. The signal is about to turn to a solid DON'T WALK.

traffic_signals.name: Pedestrian Signal — Steady DON'T WALK
traffic_signals.meaning: Do not cross. Pedestrians who have not yet left the curb must wait for the next WALK signal.

traffic_signals.name: School Zone Speed Limit Signal
traffic_signals.meaning: Flashing yellow lights on school zone speed signs indicate the 15 mph speed limit is in effect. Exceeding this speed results in 3 points and a fine.

traffic_signals.name: Railroad Crossing — Gate and Signals
traffic_signals.meaning: When gates lower and red lights flash, ALL traffic must stop. Do not go around gates. Wait until all signals stop and gates fully rise before proceeding.

scenes.name: Parallel Parking — 5-Step Method
scenes.meaning: 1. Stop even with vehicle ahead, 2 feet away. 2. Turn wheel right, back slowly toward vehicle behind. 3. As front door passes back bumper, straighten wheels. 4. When clear of vehicle ahead, turn wheels sharply left and back to vehicle behind. 5. Turn wheels right and pull to center of space.

scenes.name: School Bus Stopping Law
scenes.meaning: All vehicles must stop at least 10 feet from a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and extended stop arm. Exception: divided highway with concrete/metal barrier — opposite direction traffic may proceed with caution.

scenes.name: Truck No-Zone Blind Spots
scenes.meaning: Trucks have large blind spots on all four sides called No-Zones: front (20 feet), rear (30 feet), and both sides. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. Avoid lingering in No-Zones.

scenes.name: Truck Wide Right Turn
scenes.meaning: Trucks must make wide right turns and may swing left before turning right. Never squeeze between a turning truck and the curb. Wait for the truck to complete its turn before proceeding.

scenes.name: Splitting the Difference
scenes.meaning: When parked vehicles are on your right and oncoming vehicles are on your left, slow down and steer a middle course — splitting the difference — to maintain safe clearance on both sides.

scenes.name: Objects Adjacent — Right Hazard (Keep Left)
scenes.meaning: A hazard marker object is on the right side of the road. Chevron stripes angle downward-left, indicating you must keep to the left to avoid the obstacle.

scenes.name: Objects Adjacent — Left Hazard (Keep Right)
scenes.meaning: A hazard marker object is on the left side of the road. Chevron stripes angle downward-right, indicating you must keep to the right to avoid the obstacle.

scenes.name: Objects Adjacent — Center Hazard (Keep Left or Right)
scenes.meaning: A hazard marker is centered in or near the road. Chevron stripes alternate direction, indicating you must pass either to the left or right of the obstacle.

diagrams.name: How to Park on a Hill
diagrams.meaning: PARKING DOWNHILL with a curb: Turn wheels RIGHT (toward curb). PARKING UPHILL with a curb: Turn wheels LEFT (away from curb). DOWNHILL or UPHILL without a curb: Turn wheels RIGHT (toward road edge). Always set parking brake.

diagrams.name: Space Management — 6-Zone Cushion
diagrams.meaning: The six zones of space management around your vehicle: Zone 1 (front), Zone 2 (front-right), Zone 3 (rear-right), Zone 4 (front-left), Zone 5 (rear-left), Zone 6 (rear). Maintain space in all zones as your escape paths.

diagrams.name: Roundabout / Circular Intersection
diagrams.meaning: Approaching: slow down, yield to pedestrians at crosswalk, then yield to circulating traffic. Enter when gap exists. Travel counterclockwise. Signal right when exiting. Never stop in the roundabout — pull to the side if an emergency vehicle approaches.

diagrams.name: Jughandle Intersection
diagrams.meaning: Some commercial areas use jughandles (jug-handle turns) where a right turn lane curves back to allow left turns. Signs will indicate ALL TURNS FROM RIGHT LANE. Turn right, then use the signal light to turn left onto the main road.

diagrams.name: Left Turn — X at Intersection Center
diagrams.meaning: To avoid a tangle turn (colliding with an oncoming left-turner), imagine an X at the center of the intersection. Begin your left turn BEFORE reaching the X center so you turn into the closest lane. Never change lanes mid-turn.

diagrams.name: Intersection Lane Assignment — Dual Left Turns
diagrams.meaning: Dual left-turn lanes: both lanes turn left simultaneously. Stay in your lane throughout the turn — do not change lanes mid-turn. Watch for drivers in the adjacent lane straying into yours.

diagrams.name: Intersection Lane Assignment — Single Lane Turns
diagrams.meaning: Turn only from the lane designated for that movement. If in a right-turn-only lane, you must turn right even if you wanted to go straight.

diagrams.name: Physics of Speeding — Left-Bending Curve
diagrams.meaning: On a left-bending curve, a speeding vehicle's inertia carries it off the road to the right (off the shoulder). Slow down BEFORE entering any curve — you cannot brake effectively once in the curve.

diagrams.name: Physics of Speeding — Right-Bending Curve
diagrams.meaning: On a right-bending curve, a speeding vehicle's inertia carries it into the oncoming lane to the left. Always reduce speed before entering curves.

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Single Broken Yellow Centerline
diagrams.meaning: A single, broken yellow centerline shows the center of a two-way, two-lane road. Passing is permitted from either side when safe. You must use the lane of oncoming traffic to pass.

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Double Solid Yellow Centerline
diagrams.meaning: Double solid yellow lines — no passing permitted in either direction even without a No Passing sign.

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Solid/Broken Yellow Combination
diagrams.meaning: One solid + one broken yellow line: passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. If the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Center Turn Lane (Three-Lane Highway)
diagrams.meaning: Three-lane or five-lane highway: solid outside yellow lines mean no passing; inside broken yellow and solid yellow lines allow vehicles traveling either direction to use the center lane for left turns only.
diagrams.mutcd_code: MUTCD 3B.20 — Center Two-Way Left Turn Lane

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Multi-Lane with Broken White Lines
diagrams.meaning: Multi-lane highways without medians: broken white lines separate lanes of same-direction traffic. You may cross broken white lines to change lanes when safe; you may not cross double yellow centerlines.

diagrams.name: Pavement Marking — Divided Highway (Limited Access)
diagrams.meaning: Limited access highways with medians: right edge marked with solid white; left edge of each side marked with solid yellow; travel lanes separated by broken white lines.

diagrams.name: Vehicle Blind Spots Diagram
diagrams.meaning: Illustrates the blind spot zones around a passenger vehicle that cannot be seen in rearview or side mirrors. Always check blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

diagrams.name: Hand Signal — Left Turn
diagrams.meaning: Left arm extended horizontally out the window signals a left turn. Used when vehicle turn signals are inoperative.

diagrams.name: Hand Signal — Right Turn
diagrams.meaning: Left arm bent upward at the elbow (pointing up) out the window signals a right turn. Used when vehicle turn signals are inoperative.

diagrams.name: Hand Signal — Slow or Stop
diagrams.meaning: Left arm bent downward at the elbow (pointing down) out the window signals slowing or stopping. Used when vehicle brake lights or turn signals are inoperative.
